Apply the RO style and accessibility features to an echarts4r chart

Source: R/ro_e_standard.R
ro_e_standard.Rd

ro_e_standard() is the recommended way to finish an echarts4r chart. It applies the RO visual style with ro_e_theme() and adds all accessibility features on top. Use ro_e_theme() instead only when you need the styling without the extra accessibility features, for example for a chart type that ro_e_standard() does not cover.

Usage

ro_e_standard(
  e,
  palette = "categorical",
  fixed_aspect = TRUE,
  font = NULL,
  renderer = "svg",
  axis = NULL
)

Arguments

e

An echarts4r object (created with echarts4r::e_charts()).

palette

Character. Palette to use for series colors. One of "categorical" (default), "gender_con", or "gender_unc". Passed to ro_color_palette().

fixed_aspect

Logical. When TRUE (default), the total element (title + chart + legend) maintains a 2:1 width-to-height ratio, and the inner plot area (grid only, excluding axis labels and legend) maintains a 3:1 width-to-height ratio. Both ratios update responsively on resize. Set to FALSE to let the chart fill whatever height its container provides (useful when embedding in a fixed-size layout or a Shiny app with explicit height).

font

NULL (default) or a character string naming a system font family. When NULL, RijksoverheidSansWebText is used if installed, otherwise Verdana. Supply a font name to override both the chart labels and the custom HTML legend. A warning is issued if the font is not found on the system.

renderer

The renderer to use. One of "svg" or "canvas". Defaults to "svg" to comply with accessibility standards.

axis

Character. Arrow-key direction for tooltip navigation. One of "horizontal" (ArrowLeft / ArrowRight), "vertical" (ArrowUp / ArrowDown), or "both". Default NULL auto-detects from the chart orientation.

Value

The modified echarts4r object.

Accessibility features

  • Legend: Tab focuses legend items, Enter or Space toggles a series. Screen readers announce each item as a button with its on/off state. This is part of the legend that ro_e_theme() draws, so it is there with ro_e_theme() too.

  • Arrow keys move the tooltip across data points. The direction is auto-detected from the chart orientation (left/right for column and line charts, up/down for horizontal bar charts made with echarts4r::e_flip_coords()), or set explicitly with axis. The chart needs focus first: Tab to it or click it. Screen readers read out the tooltip content at every step.

  • Title first: screen readers announce the chart title before the axes and data. Needs renderer = "svg" (the default).

  • Axis label order: screen readers announce axis labels in axis order (left to right on the x-axis, bottom to top on the y-axis), also on time axes where ECharts draws the year label last. Needs renderer = "svg".

See also

  • ro_e_theme() for the styling only.

  • ROvis.utils::ro_color_palette() to inspect the available palettes.

Other echarts4r: ro_e_announce_title_first(), ro_e_build_keyboard_nav_js(), ro_e_build_onrender_js(), ro_e_detect_axis_orientation(), ro_e_keyboard_nav(), ro_e_keyboard_nav_axis_js(), ro_e_legend_a11y_js(), ro_e_sort_axis_labels(), ro_e_theme(), ro_e_theme_list(), ro_e_tooltip_announce_js()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(echarts4r)

data.frame(
  week = factor(rep(1:5, 2)),
  sex = rep(c("Women", "Men"), each = 5),
  n = c(12, 15, 11, 18, 20, 10, 13, 14, 16, 17)
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sex) |>
  e_charts(week) |>
  e_line(n) |>
  e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
  ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_con")
} # }
